comparison: Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find claims C1-C3, C16-C20, C23 about mechanosensory gene requirements for swallowing rhythms to be SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the conclusion could be strengthened with additional controls, while peer reviewers explicitly praised the rigorous quantification and convincing demonstration.

Perfect agreement. Both evaluations find claims C21-C22 about compensatory mechanisms (maintained ingestion rate despite lower pump frequency) to be SUPPORTED. No specific concerns were raised by either evaluation.

Perfect agreement on evaluation type (UNCERTAIN). Both evaluations find the viscosity data (C24-C25) supported but express uncertainty about the interpretations (C26-C27). OpenEval notes the functional distinction requires additional validation; peer reviewers note discrepancy with prior literature showing viscosity affects filling rather than emptying.

Agreement on SUPPORTED evaluation for genetic interaction data (C28-C31). Both evaluations accept the additive and non-additive effects as evidence for partially distinct functions, though OpenEval notes the molecular mechanism remains unclear and peer reviewers acknowledge this as part of rigorous demonstration.

Agreement on SUPPORTED evaluation for claims C42-C43 about complementary function of channels. Both evaluations accept the RNAi data showing non-additive effects. OpenEval suggests the conclusion could be strengthened by overexpression experiments; peer reviewers note this provides evidence that multiple genes may converge in common cell types.

Agreement on SUPPORTED evaluation for anatomical localization (C4-C5, C32, C38). Both evaluations accept the imaging data and genetic intersection approach. OpenEval notes some variability in neuron counting; peer reviewers confirmed the localization to specific pharyngeal mechanosensory neurons. Peer result also includes C33 about SEZ projections.

Strong disagreement. OpenEval finds claims C6-C7, C34-C35, C39-C41 about md-C necessity SUPPORTED with convergent evidence from TNT and Kir2.1 experiments. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, emphasizing a major weakness: reagents are expressed in both md-C and md-L neurons, making it insufficient to assign function to md-C alone.

Disagreement. OpenEval finds optogenetic activation data (C8, C44-C47) SUPPORTED but notes C48-C49 are speculative. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN due to the same md-C/md-L ambiguity issue - reagents are expressed in both populations, making it unclear which neurons are responsible for observed effects.

Disagreement. OpenEval finds ablation experiments (C50-C52) SUPPORTED as a well-designed control to disambiguate md-C from md-L contributions. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN, viewing reliance on this single experimental strategy (severing labellum to allow md-L degradation) as insufficient to specifically attribute defects to md-C.

Strong disagreement. OpenEval finds claims C53-C54 about stretch-sensing SUPPORTED as reasonable inference from anatomical proximity, though notes direct demonstration would strengthen it. Peer reviewers find this UNSUPPORTED, explicitly stating 'Proximity between md-C neurons and muscles is not evidence that they sense stretch.'

Agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation but different concerns. OpenEval finds calcium imaging data (C55-C56) supported but notes C57 inference may not fully recapitulate in vivo conditions. Peer reviewers raise more fundamental concerns: lack of in vivo calcium imaging traces, missing evidence that md-C responds to mechanical force, and need for positive controls in ex vivo preparation.

Agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation for GRASP data (C9, C59-C61). Both evaluations note GRASP limitations - OpenEval appropriately notes it indicates close apposition but not definitively functional synapses. Peer reviewers add concerns about GRASP false positives and questions about MN11/MN12 line expression patterns not containing motor neurons.

Agreement on UNCERTAIN evaluation for functional connectivity claims (C10, C62-C65). OpenEval notes the connection is demonstrated but whether monosynaptic/polysynaptic and precise role requires additional mapping. Peer reviewers emphasize Tmc-GAL4 expression is broader than md-C alone, so connectivity cannot be traced to md-C specifically.

Agreement on SUPPORTED evaluation for GABAA-R knockdown data (C85-C86). OpenEval notes the interpretation assumes presynaptic inhibition not directly demonstrated. Peer reviewers accepted this finding without specific critique, presenting it as supporting evidence for the circuit model.

Disagreement. OpenEval finds mechanistic interpretation (C79-C83) SUPPORTED as sound logic integrating multiple observations, though notes the model requires direct testing. Peer reviewers find this UNCERTAIN because it depends on md-C necessity claims that were insufficiently supported due to md-C/md-L ambiguity.

Both address optogenetic activation effects (C79-C81). OpenEval groups these with mechanistic inferences and finds them SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers evaluate the underlying optogenetic data as UNCERTAIN due to md-C/md-L expression ambiguity in the reagents used.

Agreement on SUPPORTED evaluation for CPG-related claims (C92-C93). OpenEval finds methylcellulose and neuronal manipulation experiments support the interpretation of pattern generator modulation by sensory input. Peer reviewers acknowledged positive impact by demonstrating mechanosensory feedback importance and providing entry point for future CPG investigation. Peer result also includes C94.

Partial overlap on claim C94. OpenEval finds speculative hypotheses (C88-C90, C94) UNCERTAIN as reasonable models lacking experimental support. Peer reviewers evaluated the broader CPG framework (C92-C93, C94) as SUPPORTED, focusing on the positive contribution to future investigation rather than the speculative nature of specific mechanisms.

Partial overlap on claim C33. OpenEval finds C33 about SEZ projections SUPPORTED based on anatomical data. Peer reviewers evaluated C33 together with other anatomical claims (C4-C5, C32, C38) as SUPPORTED, confirming localization to specific pharyngeal mechanosensory neurons.

OpenEval evaluated background claims C11-C15 about prior work on swallowing phases as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluated extensive background literature citations (C66-C78, C84, C87, C91) as SUPPORTED with appropriate references to prior work on pharyngeal sensory function, CPG properties, and motor control. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature review claims.

OpenEval evaluated background claims C36-C37 about Tmc expression in other sensory populations as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this background context justifying genetic intersection strategy.
